tested_scope: Exactly one deterministic self-local negative-control replay of the prior arbitrary-finite-turnover abstract claim/idempotency model. This replay removes exactly one assumption: authority turnover is no longer serialized with an in-flight authority-checked effect attempt. All other assumptions are retained: each authority Ai has a distinct non-reusable {Fi,Ti}; effect identity effect:E is stable; effect:E plus its durable idempotency marker are committed atomically with an uncommitted check at the effect commit point; the marker persists across turnover. The replay permits an attempt to snapshot a matching authority identity before turnover and reach the effect commit point after turnover without revalidating current authority. No public source, O/downstream/other-worker state, shared ledger, scheduler mutation, external coordinator, richer-mode arbitration, hosted compute, concrete transport, or optional second semantic leaf is modeled.

retained_assumptions: atomic uncommitted-check plus effect:E plus durable idempotency-marker commit
counterexample_schedule: A0 is current; effect:E is uncommitted.
An A0 attempt snapshots current identity A0 and observes effect:E uncommitted.
Authority turns over to A1 while the A0 attempt remains in flight.
An A1 repair attempt may also begin while effect:E is still uncommitted.
Because turnover is not serialized with the in-flight A0 attempt, A0 can reach the atomic effect commit point after A1 is already current.
If A0 linearizes first, A0 commits effect:E plus its marker even though A0 is stale; the later A1 commit attempt observes the marker and becomes a no-op. If A1 linearizes first, A0 becomes a no-op.
fixture.duplicate_effect_search: No two-commit schedule exists under this exact one-assumption removal because every effect commit still performs an atomic uncommitted check and writes the persistent effect marker in the same indivisible effect operation. Whichever contender linearizes first makes every later contender a no-op.
fixture.stronger_safety_falsification: Current-authority-only effect ownership is falsified: the schedule where A0 snapshots before turnover and commits after turnover allows a stale predecessor to produce the sole effect after A1 is current.

observations: Removing only turnover/effect serialization does not by itself break at-most-once effect safety while the atomic durable idempotency marker remains intact.
The same removal does break the stronger claim that only the currently authorized claimant can produce the effect: a predecessor can snapshot authority before turnover and commit afterward.

Therefore turnover serialization was sufficient but not necessary for duplicate suppression in the prior finite-sequence proof; it was necessary there for stale-predecessor exclusion unless replaced by commit-time authority revalidation coupled to the effect commit.
inference: Within this exact abstract model, the persistent atomic effect marker is doing the decisive work for at-most-once suppression, while serialization with turnover enforces authority correctness. This narrows the assumption set: duplicate prevention and current-authority ownership are separable properties. The result does not establish any concrete repository/API primitive, crash consistency, fork exclusion, infinite-turnover liveness, or real multi-claimant behavior.
unresolved_children: A concrete allowed zero-cost quota-independent Chat-exposed transport exposing the required durable conditional mutation semantics remains unverified.
Atomic single-winner claim acquisition and turnover keyed by stable effect identity remain unverified on a concrete allowed transport.
Fork exclusion and crash consistency under real multi-claimant contention remain unverified.

Atomicity of the uncommitted check plus effect mutation plus durable marker should be negative-controlled next because the current replay shows that assumption, rather than turnover serialization alone, is central to duplicate suppression.
If turnover is not serialized, commit-time authority revalidation coupled atomically to effect commit is required to recover current-authority-only effect ownership in this model.
